title: “Willow” Culture
synopsis: Learn about the cultural significance of the willow tree in China.

fullText.simplified:
“柳”文化

    北京冬奥会闭幕式上的“折柳送别”，体现了一种中国式的浪漫。那么关于“柳”，在汉语文化中又有哪些文化内涵呢？
    先来说说“折柳送别”。中国古代，古人在分别时，都会折柳相送。这在当时非常流行。之所以把柳树看成是离别的特殊礼物，是因为古代的客栈外经常种植大量的柳树。客栈也就是现在的酒店。人们抬头低头都是柳树，久而久之，柳树就成了一个离别的符号。再加上古诗文中有大量对柳树的描写，折柳送别慢慢就成了一种习俗了。现代人看“折柳送别”，觉得特别浪漫，特别感动，大概也是和学习了很多相关文化有关系吧！
    除了有“送别”的意思，“柳”也包含着“祝福”。柳树发芽代表春天来了，给人一种希望和美好。而且柳树生命力强，适应能力强。“折柳送别”是对朋友最好的祝福，希望朋友生活越来越好，不管去哪里都能够很快适应。
    另外，“柳”还可以表示一种思念。比如有一句诗：“月上柳梢头，人约黄昏后。”表面上写的是两个相爱的人约会的情景，暗含着诗人对妻子的思念。诗人写的是“柳梢头”，而不是“桃树、杏树”，这就能证明“柳”对古人来说，是思念的象征。
    接下来的这个意思是最有趣的：“柳”还可以指美女。中国古代，看一个女人漂亮不漂亮首先看的是她的眉毛和腰。形容眉毛是“柳叶弯眉”‘，形容一个女人腰很细，说的是她的腰“像柳条”。
    说了那么多文化内涵，再来看看关于“柳”的民俗。柳有驱邪避毒的作用。在中国古代，柳被看做是“圣木”，有驱邪的功能。柳条刚发芽的时候，将柳条插在门和窗户上，妖魔鬼怪就进不去。人们还可以把柳条戴在头上，也起到驱邪避毒的效果。现代，在清明节当天，人们也会插柳或者带柳，既是对先人的纪念，也是一种祈福，希望新一年顺利平安。
    但是，这里有个值得注意的地方：既然柳树有那么多好的意思，为什么老百姓中会流传一句话——“屋后不栽柳”呢？“屋后不栽柳”意思就是最好在房子后边不要种柳树。这是因为在中国古人的观念中，金银珠宝门前进，收在家中福气多。如果房子后边种了柳树，“柳”谐音“流”，那么金银珠宝和福气就会从房后流走，不太吉利。
    怎么样？是不是很神奇？一棵柳树都有那么多讲究！你的国家有什么有趣的树吗？它们又有什么神秘的文化呢？
fullText.traditional:
“柳”文化

    北京冬奧會閉幕式上的“折柳送別”，體現了一種中國式的浪漫。那麼關於“柳”，在漢語文化中又有哪些文化內涵呢？
    先來說說“折柳送別”。中國古代，古人在分別時，都會折柳相送。這在當時非常流行。之所以把柳樹看成是離別的特殊禮物，是因為古代的客棧外經常種植大量的柳樹。客棧也就是現在的酒店。人們抬頭低頭都是柳樹，久而久之，柳樹就成了一個離別的符號。再加上古詩文中有大量對柳樹的描寫，折柳送別慢慢就成了一種習俗了。現代人看“折柳送別”，覺得特別浪漫，特別感動，大概也是和學習了很多相關文化有關係吧！
    除了有“送別”的意思，“柳”也包含著“祝福”。柳樹發芽代表春天來了，給人一種希望和美好。而且柳樹生命力強，適應能力強。“折柳送別”是對朋友最好的祝福，希望朋友生活越來越好，不管去哪裏都能夠很快適應。
    另外，“柳”還可以表示一種思念。比如有一句詩：“月上柳梢頭，人約黃昏後。”表面上寫的是兩個相愛的人約會的情景，暗含著詩人對妻子的思念。詩人寫的是“柳梢頭”，而不是“桃樹、杏樹”，這就能證明“柳”對古人來說，是思念的象徵。
    接下來的這個意思是最有趣的：“柳”還可以指美女。中國古代，看一個女人漂亮不漂亮首先看的是她的眉毛和腰。形容眉毛是“柳葉彎眉”‘，形容一個女人腰很細，說的是她的腰“像柳條”。
    說了那麼多文化內涵，再來看看關於“柳”的民俗。柳有驅邪避毒的作用。在中國古代，柳被看做是“聖木”，有驅邪的功能。柳條剛發芽的時候，將柳條插在門和窗戶上，妖魔鬼怪就進不去。人們還可以把柳條戴在頭上，也起到驅邪避毒的效果。現代，在清明節當天，人們也會插柳或者帶柳，既是對先人的紀念，也是一種祈福，希望新一年順利平安。
    但是，這裡有個值得注意的地方：既然柳樹有那麼多好的意思，為什麼老百姓中會流傳一句話——“屋後不栽柳”呢？“屋後不栽柳”意思就是最好在房子後邊不要種柳樹。這是因為在中國古人的觀念中，金銀珠寶門前進，收在家中福氣多。如果房子後邊種了柳樹，“柳”諧音“流”，那麼金銀珠寶和福氣就會從房後流走，不太吉利。
    怎麼樣？是不是很神奇？一棵柳樹都有那麼多講究！你的國家有什麼有趣的樹嗎？它們又有什麼神秘的文化呢？

sentences.simplified: “屋后不栽柳”意思就是最好在房子后边不要种柳树。
sentences.traditional: “屋後不栽柳”意思就是最好在房子後邊不要種柳樹。
sentences.pinyin: wū hòu bù zāi liǔ yì si jiù shì zuì hǎo zài fáng zi hòu bian bú yào zhòng liǔ shù
sentences.english: .. why is there a saying among the people: “Don’t plant willow behind the house”?

sentences.simplified: 这是因为在中国古人的观念中，金银珠宝门前进，收在家中福气多。
sentences.traditional: 這是因為在中國古人的觀念中，金銀珠寶門前進，收在家中福氣多。
sentences.pinyin: zhè shì yīn wèi zài zhōng guó gǔ rén de guān niàn zhōng jīn yín zhū bǎo mén qián jìn shōu zài jiā zhōng fú qi duō
sentences.english: “Don’t plant willow behind the house“ means that it’s advisable not to plant willow trees behind a house.

sentences.simplified: 如果房子后边种了柳树，
sentences.traditional: 如果房子後邊種了柳樹，
sentences.pinyin: rú guǒ fáng zi hòu bian zhòng le liǔ shù
sentences.english: This is because people in ancient China believed that money and treasures came in through the door, bringing much good fortune.

sentences.simplified: “柳”谐音“流”，那么金银珠宝和福气就会从房后流走，不太吉利。
sentences.traditional: “柳”諧音“流”，那麼金銀珠寶和福氣就會從房後流走，不太吉利。
sentences.pinyin: liǔ xié yīn liú nà me jīn yín zhū bǎo hé fú qi jiù huì cóng fáng hòu liú zǒu bú tài jí lì
sentences.english: If a willow tree is planted behind the house, ..
.. because ”willow” sounds like “flow”, the money and treasures will flow out from the back of the house, which is not auspicious.

sentences.simplified: 怎么样？是不是很神奇？一棵柳树都有那么多讲究！
sentences.traditional: 怎麼樣？是不是很神奇？一棵柳樹都有那麼多講究！
sentences.pinyin: zěn me yàng shì bú shì hěn shén qí yì kē liǔ shù dōu yǒu nà me duō jiǎng jiu

sentences.simplified: 你的国家有什么有趣的树吗？它们又有什么神秘的文化呢？
sentences.traditional: 你的國家有什麼有趣的樹嗎？它們又有什麼神秘的文化呢？
sentences.pinyin: nǐ de guó jiā yǒu shén me yǒu qù de shù ma tā men yòu yǒu shén me shén mì de wén huà ne
sentences.english: What do you think? Isn’t this mysterious? There are so many things to think about behind a willow tree.

sentence_translations: “Willow” Culture
The “breaking of the willow to bid farewell” at the Beijing Winter Olympics closing ceremony embodied a Chinese style of romance.
So, what is the significance of ”willow” in Chinese culture?
First, let’s talk about the “breaking of the willow to bid farewell“.
In ancient China, when people parted ways, they would break willows to send each other off.
This was very popular at the time.
Willow trees were seen as a special parting gift because large numbers of willow trees were often planted outside taverns in ancient times.
These taverns were like today’s hotels. Whether people looked up or down, they would see willow trees everywhere.
Over time, willow trees became a symbol of parting.
In addition, ancient poems and literature often included depictions of willow trees.
The breaking of the willow to bid farewell gradually became a custom.
When modern people see the “breaking of the willow to bid farewell”, they feel that this gesture is very romantic and touching.
It’s likely that this is also because they have studied a lot of related culture!
In addition to meaning “farewell”, “willow” also has the meaning of “blessings”.
The sprouting of willows represents the arrival of spring, bringing people a sense of hope and joy.
Willow trees are also very vigorous and adaptable.
The “breaking of the willow to bid farewell” is the best blessing to give friends.
It’s a wish that their lives will get better and better and that they will be able to adapt quickly no matter where they go.
Additionally, “willow” can represent a type of longing.
For instance, there is a line in a poem: “The moon rose above the willow branch tips, the lovers met after twilight”.
On the surface, the poem writes about two lovers on a date. The implicit meaning is the poet’s feelings of longing for his wife.
The poet writes about “willow branch tips”, rather than “peach trees” or “apricot trees”.
This proves that the ”willow” was a symbol of longing for ancient people.
This next meaning is the most interesting one: the “willow” can also represent beautiful women.
In ancient China, to determine whether a woman was beautiful or not, one first looked at her eyebrows and waist.
The phrase that describes eyebrows is “eyebrows curved like a willow leaf”.
A woman’s thin waist can be described as “like a willow branch”.
After talking through all this cultural significance, let’s look at some traditional customs relating to the “willow”.
The willow has the effect of warding off evil and removing toxins.
In ancient China, the willow was regarded as a “sacred wood” that could ward off evil.
If newly sprouted willow branches were inserted into doors and windows, demons and ghosts could no longer enter.
People could also wear willow branches on their heads, which also had the effect of warding off evil.
In modern times, people will also plant willow or bring willow on the day of the Qingming Festival.
This acts both as a tribute to their ancestors and also as a prayer for a safe and smooth new year.
But, there is something noteworthy here: if the willow tree has so many good meanings, ..
.. why is there a saying among the people: “Don’t plant willow behind the house”?
“Don’t plant willow behind the house“ means that it’s advisable not to plant willow trees behind a house.
This is because people in ancient China believed that money and treasures came in through the door, bringing much good fortune.
If a willow tree is planted behind the house, ..
.. because ”willow” sounds like “flow”, the money and treasures will flow out from the back of the house, which is not auspicious.
What do you think? Isn’t this mysterious? There are so many things to think about behind a willow tree.
Does your country have any interesting trees? What mysterious cultural meaning do they have?
